name: Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Joint Keratoses
aliases: Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Articular Keratoses
Localized Palmoplantar Hyperkeratosis with Joint Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Joint Keratoses

criteria.description: Presence of focal hyperkeratotic plaques localized to the palms and/or soles
Development of keratotic lesions overlying interphalangeal and other peripheral joints
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis and absence of epidermolytic changes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
No evidence of systemic or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and keratotic joint lesions confirmed by histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and histopathological; genetic testing may aid but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal hyperkeratotic plaques on palms and soles
searchTerms: thickened rough skin patches on hands and feet
hard skin plaques on palms and soles
raised thick skin areas on hands and feet
thick skin bumps over finger joints

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized thickening of the stratum corneum without blistering
searchTerms: localized thick skin layer without blisters
small cracks in thickened skin plaques

common.symptomName: Pain or discomfort at sites of keratotic joint lesions
Callus formation on pressure points of palms and soles
searchTerms: calluses on pressure points of hands and feet
hardened skin spots on palms and soles
thick skin buildup at pressure sites
mild redness around thick skin plaques
faint skin redness by keratotic areas

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness adjacent to keratotic lesions
searchTerms: mild joint stiffness near thickened skin
slight joint tightness next to plaques
joint stiffness adjacent to skin lesions

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of fissured plaques

searchTerms: excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Nail dystrophy associated with adjacent keratoderma

rare.symptomName: Mild joint swelling without systemic arthritis
searchTerms: localized joint swelling without systemic symptoms

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
imaging: X-rays of affected joints typically normal or show mild soft tissue thickening
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic focal keratoderma and joint keratoses

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epidermolytic changes on histology
Diffuse rather than focal palmoplantar involvement
Multiple small punctate keratoses rather than focal plaques
Later onset in adolescence or adulthood

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Signs of systemic arthritis or inflammatory joint disease
Secondary infection with cellulitis or abscess formation
